findings.title: Missing upper bound validation on num_parameters for Channel audio elements
findings.message: In audio_element_obu(), the num_parameters value is read from untrusted input via ffio_read_leb() without an upper bound check when audio_element_type is 0 (Channel representations). The IAMF specification allows at most 2 parameters for Channel representations (DEMIXING and RECON_GAIN), but the code only validates that num_parameters must be 0 for Scene representations (audio_element_type != 0). A crafted IAMF file can supply num_parameters > 2, causing the subsequent loop to call param_parse() with duplicate parameter types. When the same parameter type (e.g., DEMIXING) is parsed multiple times, the pointer in element->demixing_info or element->recon_gain_info is overwritten by a new allocation from av_iamf_param_definition_alloc(), leaking the previously allocated memory. This leads to uncontrolled memory consumption (memory leak) which can be exploited for denial of service. This is CVE-2025-1816.
findings.suggestion: Add a constraint check that rejects num_parameters > 2 when audio_element_type is 0 (Channel representations), since the IAMF spec only defines two valid parameter types (DEMIXING and RECON_GAIN) for channel-based audio elements.

ground_truth.root_cause: Missing input validation: the code does not enforce the IAMF specification's constraint that Channel audio elements can have at most 2 parameters. The existing validation only checks that Scene representations have 0 parameters, but does not limit the count for Channel representations.
